title: Chapter 3: The map of the water
licence: Original sample written for this project
text: Pim let Ines into the warden house through the coal hatch after the lamps were put out. He asked for nothing except that she teach him to read the tree marks, which no one had ever bothered to show him, and she agreed. They found the map chest under Oskar's desk. The chest was already open, and the water map was gone. In its place lay a letter bearing the seal of Corvin Asche. The letter thanked Oskar for the loan of the map and promised to cancel his debt of ninety silver marks once the purchases were complete. Ines understood that Oskar had borrowed from Asche and had paid him with the map. She put the letter inside her coat. As they were leaving, Oskar came in carrying a candle. Pim hid in the coal bin, but Ines was caught in the open. Oskar saw the empty chest and the broken wax on her sleeve. He did not call for help. Instead he sat down and told her that his wife had been ill for two winters and that the physicians in Peyre had taken every coin he had. Asche had offered the loan when no one in Halden would. Oskar said he had believed the merchant only wanted to survey the land. Ines told him that three more trees would be dead by morning. Oskar was silent for a long while. Then he said that he had copied part of the map as a young man, and he gave her the copy from the lining of his coat. The copy showed a stair behind the old mill that led down to the spring gate. Half of it had been torn away, so the paths beyond the gate were missing. Oskar would not go with her, because Asche would hear of it and call in the debt.
